content: Cefaclor, USP, is a semisynthetic antibiotic belonging to the cephalosporin class, designed for oral administration. Its chemical name is 3-chloro-7-D-(2-phenylglycinamido)-3-cephem-4-carboxylic acid monohydrate. The molecular formula of cefaclor is C15H14ClN3O4S·H2O, and its molecular weight is 385.82. Each 250 mg capsule of cefaclor contains cefaclor monohydrate, which is equivalent to 250 mg (0.68 mmol) of anhydrous cefaclor. The inactive ingredients in the 250 mg capsule include magnesium stearate, sodium starch glycolate, lactose monohydrate, and talc. The capsule shell is composed of gelatin, titanium dioxide, and imprinting ink, which contains shellac, strong ammonia solution, potassium hydroxide, black iron oxide, dehydrated alcohol, isopropyl alcohol, butyl alcohol, and propylene glycol. Each 500 mg capsule of cefaclor contains cefaclor monohydrate, which is equivalent to 500 mg (1.36 mmol) of anhydrous cefaclor. The inactive ingredients in the 500 mg capsule include magnesium stearate, sodium starch glycolate, lactose monohydrate, and talc. The capsule shell is made of gelatin, titanium dioxide, and imprinting ink, which contains shellac, strong ammonia solution, titanium dioxide, aluminum lake, dehydrated alcohol, isopropyl alcohol, butyl alcohol, and propylene glycol.
